title: A card answered from its own origin is refused when the app has an older session
body:
## Summary
`_decision_ctx` judges a card's replay under the first session whose app id matches, not under the origin that answered, so when one app has registered from two origins a card filed and answered on the pinned origin is refused `foreign_origin`.

## Description
src/athena/daemon/routes.py:1003-1035 builds the replay context's `page_origin` as `next(s.origin for s in daemon.sessions.all() if s.app_id == app_id)` - the first origin that ever registered the app, in dictionary order. Policy rule 3 (src/athena/harness/policy.py:210-217) compares that against `pinned_origins[app]`, which `AthenaDaemon.pin` moves to the latest origin to post a manifest (src/athena/daemon/server.py:283-296). `decide` already reads the answering `origin` off the body and checks it is a live session of the card's app (`_origin_refusal`, routes.py:977-1000), then throws it away. The docstring says the replay sees "the page origin that app's manifest was published from"; it sees whichever came first. Fixed looks like: the replay is judged under the stated origin when one is given (validated as today), the first session only when none is. That turns one refusal into a permit (a card answered from the pinned origin), and also permits a card filed on A and answered from B once B holds the pin, which is why this is not built here. Registry: agent-browser-control/socket-scoped-surface is not it; the repo's own rule 3 is.

## Flow
- an app registers from http://localhost:3001, then from http://localhost:3002 (same app id; the shell now also admits 127.0.0.1, ADR 0119) -> the pin moves to :3002
- a turn on :3002 files a gated card; the person approves it from :3002
- -> decide -> _decision_ctx picks :3001 (first session) -> rule 3: pinned :3002 != :3001 -> 409 foreign_origin
- fix, in build order: a daemon test with two origins for one app (both orders), then `_decision_ctx(stated=...)`, then decide which of the two orders the operator wants permitted

## Expected impact
Whoever runs one app on two local ports or on localhost and 127.0.0.1 stops seeing their own approvals refused. Could break: a card filed on the old origin and answered from the new one would execute where today it is refused - the operator's call.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a card is judged under the origin that answered it
Before: probe (2026-10-16, routes called in-process): A registers, B registers, card filed on B and answered from B -> 409 foreign_origin "published its manifest from 'http://localhost:3002' and this session is on 'http://localhost:3001'"; card filed on A, B registers, answered from A -> 409 (the same)
After: predicted: the first -> 200 approved; the second -> 409 still (A is not the pin)
Method: probe for Before; After not built because it changes what an approved card may run on in one of the two orders
Result: better
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence:
src/athena/daemon/routes.py:1022-1025 page_origin = next((s.origin for s in daemon.sessions.all() if s.app_id == app_id), None)
src/athena/harness/policy.py:210-211 expected = self.pinned_origins.get(app_id); if expected is not None and ctx.page_origin is not None and ctx.page_origin != expected
probe output: pin: http://localhost:3002 card filed on: http://localhost:3002 / decide: 409 foreign_origin origin_pinning ... this session is on 'http://localhost:3001'

title: A spoken decline is ledgered as surface panel
body:
## Summary
The voice gateway answers a card through `routes.decide`, whose replay context hard-codes `surface="panel"`, so a refusal or decline spoken on /voice writes its ledger row under `panel`.

## Description
src/athena/daemon/routes.py:1031 (`_decision_ctx`) sets `surface="panel"` and the lane's refusal row records `surface=ctx.surface` (src/athena/lane/browser_lane.py:445). src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:991-1002 builds a Request and calls `decide` with `choice`, `origin` and `disabled_origins` and no surface. `turn_context`'s own docstring (routes.py:779-781) says a spoken turn and a typed one differ in exactly `surface` and `trigger`, the two words the ledger rolls up by; the decision path loses one of them. Fixed: `decide` reads an optional `surface` from the body (a member of the surfaces the ledger knows, else `panel`) and the gateway sends `voice`.

## Flow
- a spoken "no" to a waiting card -> gateway._answer -> routes.decide
- -> _decision_ctx(surface="panel") -> lane._row(surface=ctx.surface)
- -> GET /ledger/rollup?by=surface counts the voice decline under panel

## Expected impact
The ledger's per-surface rollup stops undercounting voice. Could break: nothing reads the decline row's surface for a decision today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a decision's ledger row names the surface that answered it
Before: read from the code path (three sites above); no voice decline test asserts the row's surface
After: predicted: a test in tests/channels/test_voice_gateway.py that declines by voice sees one row with surface voice
Method: simulation - the fix needs src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py, which belongs to voice-channel
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/daemon/routes.py:1031 surface="panel",
src/athena/lane/browser_lane.py:445 surface=ctx.surface,
src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:994-1001 body={"choice": ..., "origin": ..., "disabled_origins": ...} (no surface)
instrument: tests/channels/test_voice_gateway.py: a spoken decline of a card writes one ledger row whose surface is voice; red today (panel), green once decide takes an optional surface and the gateway sends it

title: Every origin ever registered keeps its session, pin and tools for the daemon's life
body:
## Summary
Nothing in the daemon ever forgets a page: `Sessions.drop` and `Catalog.drop_origin` have no production caller, so each web origin the shell ever offered a manifest for keeps its session, its pin and its tools (at least the nine hands) until the process ends.

## Description
ADR 0065 has the shell publish the hands for every tab with an origin the daemon admits, so every distinct https site opened in the shell adds a session (src/athena/daemon/sessions.py:85-120), a pin (src/athena/daemon/server.py:283-296) and nine catalog entries (`merge_manifest`). `Sessions.drop` (src/athena/daemon/sessions.py:122-126) and `Catalog.drop_origin` (src/athena/core/catalog.py:382) exist and are tested, and no route or shell event calls either. `/health` counts the sessions and tools that never leave, `_decision_ctx` scans every session per answer, and a pin outlives the tab it was made for. Fixed looks like: an unregister act (a route the shell calls on tab close, or an idle bound) that drops the session and the origin's tools together and decides what happens to the pin. That is a design call the round does not make.

## Flow
- open N distinct https sites in the shell -> N hands manifests -> N sessions, N pins, 9N entries
- close every tab -> GET /health still reports N sessions and the tools
- fix, in build order: a test that registers and unregisters an origin and counts sessions and catalog entries, then the act

## Expected impact
A daemon that runs all day stops growing with browsing. Could break: a pin dropped with its session makes rule 3 compare nothing for that app until it registers again.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - registered state is bounded by the open tabs, not the history
Before: read: zero production callers (grep below); per origin +1 session, +1 pin, +9 entries
After: predicted: after close, 0 sessions and 0 entries for that origin
Method: simulation - the unregister act's trigger and the pin's fate are design calls
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
git grep -n "drop_origin\|sessions.drop\|\.drop(" -- src apps/desktop/src packages (definitions excluded) -> only voice player drops; no daemon caller
tests/core/test_catalog.py:213 is the only caller of drop_origin
instrument: tests/daemon: register K hands manifests from K origins, unregister them through the new act, assert len(daemon.sessions) and len(daemon.catalog) return to the baseline; today there is no act, so the count only grows

title: The minted token file is written with default permissions and chmod-ed after
body:
## Summary
`resolve_token` writes the minted token with `Path.write_text` and only then `chmod(0o600)`, so on POSIX the file exists with the umask's mode (usually 0644) for a moment, and a pre-existing file keeps whatever mode it had until the chmod.

## Description
src/athena/daemon/server.py:713-719 (`path.write_text(json.dumps({"token": minted}))` then `path.chmod(0o600)` under `suppress(OSError)`). Another local user can open the file between the two calls and keep the descriptor; the token is the whole authorization story of a loopback daemon (registry agent-browser-control/socket-scoped-surface: a bearer token in an owner-only file). Fixed: create it with `os.open(path, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0o600)` (and write to a temp file then replace, so a reader never sees a half-written token). On Windows the user's profile is the protection, as the code says, so nothing changes there.

## Flow
- first `athena serve` with no daemon.json -> write_text creates it 0644 -> chmod 0600
- a second local user polling the path opens it in the window and reads the token
- fix: os.open with mode 0o600 at creation, then os.replace

## Expected impact
Closes a race on multi-user POSIX machines. Could break: nothing; the mode is the same once written.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the token file is never readable by another user, not even briefly
Before: read from the code; not reproducible on this Windows build machine
After: predicted: a POSIX test that stats the file right after creation sees 0600
Method: simulation - the window exists only on POSIX and this round ran on Windows
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
src/athena/daemon/server.py:715 path.write_text(json.dumps({"token": minted}), encoding="utf-8")
src/athena/daemon/server.py:718-719 with suppress(OSError): path.chmod(0o600)
instrument: tests/daemon/test_server.py, POSIX only (skip on win32): monkeypatch os.open/Path.write_text to record the mode the file is created with; resolve_token must create it 0o600 (red today: created with the umask's mode, chmod-ed after)

title: The OAuth callback server binds with address reuse on Windows
body:
## Summary
The connector consent flow's one-shot callback server is a plain `HTTPServer`, which binds with `SO_REUSEADDR`; on Windows another process asking for reuse can bind the same port and receive the authorization code.

## Description
src/athena/connectors/oauth.py:111 `HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), ...)` inherits `allow_reuse_address = 1`. This round measured the same class on the daemon's own server (a second socket with SO_REUSEADDR bound a listening port on this Windows machine) and fixed it with `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` in `DaemonServer` (src/athena/daemon/server.py). The callback server carries the OAuth `code` and `state` on its one request. Fixed: the same exclusive bind (subclass or reuse `DaemonServer`'s `server_bind`). The file belongs to connector-service.

## Flow
- a consent flow opens the callback server on 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>
- a process that learns the port binds it with SO_REUSEADDR (allowed on Windows)
- the browser's redirect may be delivered to that process with the code

## Expected impact
Same-machine defence in depth for the consent flow. Could break: nothing; the port is ephemeral and used once.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - nobody else can bind the callback port
Before: probe on the daemon's server class (same stdlib base): second bind succeeded on Windows before this round's fix
After: predicted: a test that binds a SO_REUSEADDR socket on the flow's port fails to bind
Method: probe on the sibling class; the file is outside this round's write set
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
src/athena/connectors/oauth.py:111 self._server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), _make_handler(self))
probe (2026-10-16, Windows): DaemonServer before the fix -> SECOND BIND SUCCEEDED on 55899
instrument: tests/connectors/test_oauth.py: start a flow, then bind a socket with SO_REUSEADDR on its redirect port; the bind must fail (red today on Windows)

title: GET /playbooks opens one read connection per item to count its citations
body:
## Summary
`playbooks` calls `brain.sources_of(memory.id)` once per item, and each call opens and closes its own read-only SQLite connection, so a page of 200 opens 200 connections.

## Description
src/athena/daemon/routes.py:1157 `"citations": len(daemon.brain.sources_of(memory.id))` inside the list comprehension; src/athena/core/brain/store.py:394-400 `sources_of` is `with closing(self.read_connection())` per call (WAL pragmas included). One grouped `SELECT node_id, COUNT(*) ... WHERE node_id IN (...) GROUP BY node_id` on one read connection answers the same counts. No desktop code calls GET /playbooks today (grep below), which caps the impact.

## Flow
- GET /playbooks?origin=<o>&limit=200 with 200 procedurals distilled
- -> recall, then 200 x (open read connection, one SELECT, close)

## Expected impact
Cheaper reads for a future panel poller. Could break: nothing, the counts are the same.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one read connection per page, not per item
Before: read from the code: limit+1 connections per call (limit up to 200)
After: predicted: 1 connection per call; time at limit=200 to be measured
Method: simulation - no consumer polls this route today, so the round did not build the timing harness
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/daemon/routes.py:1157 "citations": len(daemon.brain.sources_of(memory.id)),
src/athena/core/brain/store.py:395 with closing(self.read_connection()) as con:
grep '/playbooks' apps/desktop/src (non-test) -> only a static image path
instrument: a timing probe over a brain with 200 procedurals: GET /playbooks?limit=200 wall time and connection count (wrap Brain.read_connection) before and after a grouped count

title: Admit http://127.0.0.1 as a page origin beside localhost (owner call)
body:
## Summary
Decide whether a page served on http://127.0.0.1:<port> may register tools, as http://localhost:<port> may.

## Description
The page-origin rule (src/athena/contracts/manifest.py page_origin_admitted, mirrored by apps/desktop/src/lib/manifest.ts registrable; ADR 0119) admits plain http only on host localhost. 127.0.0.1 reaches the same local server and the shell already allows both spellings for its own UI (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/daemon.rs), so a dev server opened by IP is refused for no security reason. Admitting it widens who may register tools, so it is an owner call, not a sweep fix.

## Flow
- add "127.0.0.1" to LOOPBACK_PAGE_HOSTS in manifest.py and manifest.ts
- move the http://127.0.0.1:3001 row from PAGE_ORIGINS_REFUSED to PAGE_ORIGINS_ADMITTED in tests/contracts/test_manifest.py; both sides read that table
- amend ADR 0119 decision 2

## Expected impact
A page served by IP registers like its localhost twin. Could break: nothing in the tree serves on 127.0.0.1 today.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a local page opened by IP can register its tools
Before: http://127.0.0.1:3001 refused on both sides (table row, 15c4eee)
After: admitted on both sides, one row moved
Method: gate - the shared table decides it both ways
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence: src/athena/contracts/manifest.py LOOPBACK_PAGE_HOSTS; apps/desktop/src/lib/manifest.ts LOOPBACK_PAGE_HOSTS; tests/contracts/test_manifest.py PAGE_ORIGINS_REFUSED; 518fc33 admitted it, 15c4eee restored the refusal
